To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exchange rate regimes have a strong influence on trade policies in transition economies.

the exchange rate has played a key role in the determination of trade policy in transition economies and that the adoption of a floating exchange rate regime would be beneficial to all the countries examined in this paper.

the exchange rate regimes and commercial policy of transition economies are closely linked, and the exchange rates of these countries have been overvalued for a long period, resulting in a decline of competitiveness and an increase of protection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the nominal and real exchange rate and trade policy.

three main issues: the relationship between exchange rates and commercial policies in the six economies examined; the impact of exchange rate policies on commercial policy and vice versa; and the impact of exchange rates on the trade performance of these economies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the exchange rate regime in the six countries studied is not the main factor influencing the level of protection afforded domestic producers, and that it is not a major determinant of trade policy in these countries.
exchange rates have not played the central role in the process of adjustment in the six countries studied.
the exchange rate is not a good instrument for trade policy, but it may be used for that purpose if it is managed flexibly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transition economies have not been able to use exchange rate policy as a means of protecting domestic industry.

we have demonstrated the importance of the exchange rate in influencing the trade policy stance in transition economies and that the adoption of a more flexible nominal exchange rate would reduce the need for governments to resort to trade barriers.
the exchange rate regimes of the six economies have had a negative impact on their commercial policy and that a greater degree of flexibility would be beneficial.
The main takeaway from our work is that
exchange rate regimes are an important determinant of the trade policy environment.
there is no one-size-fits-all solution to the exchange rate problem in transition economies.
exchange rate management can play a useful role in stabilizing trade policy.
